title: Repository app-surface proof integration readiness governance
purpose: Define how future app-surface change classes map to Dev, Test, Compose, Staging, acceptance proof, and retained artifacts before UI implementation begins, without implementing an app surface or claiming readiness.

nonClaims: No route, screen, UI adapter, Expo app, Next app, generated client, or browser E2E implementation is created.
No staging readiness, product UI readiness, production readiness, deployment readiness, store readiness, release readiness, live-provider readiness, or human-acceptance completion claim is made.
Staging is not the default proof path for app-surface work.

proofRoutingRules: Every app-surface change starts with the lowest sufficient proof level and escalates only when the changed behaviour crosses a contract, provider, public route, staging, or human-acceptance boundary.
In-memory or Dev proof cannot satisfy provider-backed Compose proof when provider semantics matter.
Test proof remains Test proof and does not imply staging readiness.
Generated reports, screenshots, and external-review bundles are supporting artifacts and cannot upgrade raw evidence, proof level, environment, or provider mode.
Ambiguous app-surface impact falls back to fuller affected-family validation rather than defaulting to staging or passing silently.
Fresh proof-cockpit machine QA remains a terminal orchestration concern unless a later material issue explicitly requires earlier collection.
artifactExpectations: route proof map for implemented routes or screens
contract conformance output when contracts or generated clients are consumed
provider-mode and environment labels for provider-backed flows
screenshot retention class and source reference for visual artifacts
evidence freshness and custody references for proof-supporting artifacts
non-claim statement for every generated report or projection

realisedPreUiGateCoverage.realisation: The tests-required-before-UI and test-suite parent planning gates are realised for bounded local app-surface implementation by repository-test-suite-governance.json and repository-optimisation-realisation-semantics.json. Actual implementation still runs the applicable test and validator gates for the changed files.

The final owner decision gate is realised by docs/architecture/pre-ui-repository-readiness-realisation.json for bounded local app-surface implementation only. It does not claim store, CDN, privacy, external review, staging, live-provider, or production readiness.

acceptanceCriteriaTrace.criterion: Readiness plan maps app-surface change classes to required proof and artifacts.

Readiness checklist states required contracts, generation rules, validation, and owner decisions.

appSurfaceWorkloadForecast.scope: Forecast only for future Expo and Next app-surface work. This does not authorise UI implementation, package creation, route creation, app creation, or readiness claims.
packageClasses: Expo application workspace package and mobile runtime dependencies if approved later.
Next application workspace package and web runtime dependencies if approved later.
Shared UI, generated API client, and app-surface test helper packages only if separately authorised.
Build, transpilation, bundling, and native-tooling dependencies introduced by app-surface work.
Contract, type generation, browser, and mobile test dependencies needed to prove app-surface behaviour.
commandImpact: Frozen install and lockfile validation become more sensitive to workspace breadth and generator inputs.
Typecheck, lint, unit, contract, generated-client conformance, and app build commands may need separate cache keys and failure surfaces.
Future Expo and Next commands must route through the current command-surface target governance before becoming preferred entry points.
Proof commands must continue to distinguish hermetic mock, live external provider, production shaped, and production live dimensions.
artifactImpact: Package-manager store and build caches need keys covering package manifests, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml, package-manager version, overrides, and allow-build settings.
Generated clients, build outputs, screenshots, logs, coverage, and validation evidence need retention, naming, size-control, and source-traceability rules.
Generated reports remain lower authority than raw evidence and semantic definitions.
Large app-surface artifacts should use manifest-first scanning and avoid unconditional deep artifact walks.
ciCostImpact: Cold install cost can increase with additional workspace packages, native toolchains, generator dependencies, and browser/mobile test dependencies.
Warm cache cost depends on stable cache keys that include workspace, lockfile, package manager, generator, contract, and build configuration inputs.
App build and browser/mobile test stages should remain bounded and separate from foundation validation until promoted by an approved directive.
Unknown or unmeasured CI impact must not be hidden by narrowed validation; it falls back to the full relevant gate.
proofLadderImpact: Future UI proof must compare observed workload against this forecast and update gates before claiming readiness.
Dev, Test, and Staging evidence remain separate proof environments and cannot be upgraded by generated reports.
Hermetic mock proof does not satisfy live external provider proof, and production shaped does not satisfy production live.
Missing app-surface evidence, stale generated output, unknown provider mode, or environment mismatch must fail closed.

generatedClientPipelineReadinessGate.scope: Readiness checklist only. This does not create a generated client, generated artifact, schema, package, route, or UI consumer.
requiredContracts: Source contracts used for generation must be active or otherwise explicitly authorised by USF semantic authority.
Planned schemas alone must not be used as generated-client authority.
Contract source hashes, lifecycle state, generator inputs, and output manifest references must be retained with validation evidence.
Generated-client consumers must trace to the exact source contract and generated output they consume.
generationRules: Generator version, package-manager version, lockfile state, workspace state, source contract hash, build configuration, and environment dimensions are required cache-key inputs.
Generation must be reproducible or must record an explicit bounded non-determinism comparison rule before use.
Generated outputs are projections, not semantic authority, and cannot upgrade readiness claims.
Unknown generator input, missing source hash, stale output, schema lifecycle mismatch, or missing retention evidence fails closed.
validationRules: Contract-conformance validation must compare generated clients against the governed source contract used to generate them.
Validation must fail stale generated output, missing generator metadata, lifecycle mismatch, unknown source contract, or missing raw evidence.
Generated-client validation evidence must remain distinct from generated reports and source implementation.
UI consumption requires source-to-output traceability, conformance evidence, artifact retention, and owner approval where required.
ownerDecisionChecklist: Decide the allowed generator and generated-output retention model before implementation.
Decide whether generated outputs are committed, retained as artifacts, or rebuilt from retained source inputs.
Decide cache invalidation ownership for source contract, schema lifecycle, generator, package manager, lockfile, workspace, and build configuration changes.
Decide the owner approval path for UI consumption of generated clients.
Decide how generated-client failures block app-surface readiness without treating generated output as authority.

requiredValidators: Validator regression-proofing gate for stale input, missing input, invalid JSON, unknown controlled values, generated-report non-authority, and omitted path classes.
Validator rule-to-authority traceability gate so UI-facing semantics trace to USF semantic definitions, ADRs, validator rules, and proof expectations rather than implementation resemblance.
Generated-client contract conformance and lifecycle gate before UI consumes generated clients.
App-surface proof routing gate for provider mode, environment, proof level, and retained artifact expectations.
Stale evidence and generated-report non-authority detection gate for UI proof artifacts.
Aggregate validator command manifest and before-after validator equivalence gate for any command routing, caching, partial-run, or optimisation change before UI work.
optionalValidators: Property-based validator test pilots for controlled vocabularies, taxonomy uniqueness, schema lifecycle, evidence status, and provider/environment separation.
Secret and environment leakage scans for UI proof artifacts after scope, owner, false-positive handling, and rollback are defined.
Duplicate-content and stale-guidance checks as repository-hygiene support, not UI semantic authority.
validationExpectations: Future UI implementation gate must run validator selftests and planted-defect suites for any validator family affected by UI semantics, generated clients, evidence artifacts, or command routing.

Future UI gate must fail closed on unknown validator ownership, stale generated output, missing raw evidence, missing source contract hash, schema lifecycle mismatch, provider-mode mismatch, environment mismatch, or generated-report-only proof.
Any validator optimisation or affected-only run before UI work must compare against full validation or documented before-after validator equivalence evidence.
No validator gap may be treated as UI-ready solely because a discovery artifact exists; implementation gates require actual validation evidence when implementation begins.

requiredChangesIdentified: Preserve current preferred command entry points and compatibility aliases before adding app-surface commands.
Keep aggregate validator command manifest and command-surface target governance as the routing source for future UI-related commands.
Resolve repository structure and large-file audit evidence requirements before treating the repository as UI-implementation ready.
Keep package graph, workspace, generated-client, and build-artifact policies in force before adding Expo, Next, browser, mobile, or generated-client packages.
Preserve developer and AI-agent proof-ladder guidance so UI work does not default to staging proof or readiness claims.

USF-695 evidence is captured by repository-artifact-storage-and-naming-governance.json and remains an evidence boundary for storage migration claims.

validationProofExpectation: Future UI implementation must not begin from workspace globs, package names, or command aliases alone.
Future UI command additions must include command manifest and validator routing review.
Unknown repository/tooling impact must fail closed to full relevant gates and owner decision.

requiredChangesIdentified: Generated clients and build artifacts must preserve source contract hashes, generator metadata, lifecycle state, and cache-key inputs.
Large app-surface artifacts need manifest-first scanning, retention class, freshness state, and generated-report non-authority markers.
Package, build, TypeScript, generated-client, screenshot, log, and proof evidence caches need explicit invalidation inputs before readiness claims.
Compose proof evidence reuse requires validator-checkable handoff records before later Test or Staging steps can rely on it.
Staging rehearsal evidence packs must distinguish raw evidence, retained proof artifacts, generated reports, custody, environment, provider mode, and proof level.
evidenceBoundaries: USF-695 is covered as current evidence in repository-artifact-storage-and-naming-governance.json; storage migration still requires reference-resolution proof.
USF-853 evaluation is approved for all storage options; selected migration still requires custody, access, rollback, and evidence-preservation proof.
USF-985 and USF-986 are handoff schema and validator implementation boundaries for promotion claims, not evidence requirements to bounded local app-surface implementation.
USF-982 is covered by repository-optimisation-realisation-semantics.json for bounded local implementation; promotion workflow readiness remains a separate evidence claim.
validationProofExpectation: Future UI artifact and cache changes must fail closed on stale output, missing source hash, unknown generator input, missing custody, environment mismatch, provider-mode mismatch, or generated-report-only proof.
Future artifact pruning or migration requires retention, owner approval where needed, and reference-resolution validation.
Future UI screenshots and generated reports cannot upgrade readiness without underlying raw evidence or retained proof artifacts.

requiredChangesIdentified: Dev, Test, Compose-backed proof, Staging rehearsal, production-shaped proof, production-live proof, and human acceptance must remain separate proof states.
Provider mode and environment must remain separate dimensions and cannot upgrade each other by implication.
The staging rehearsal evidence pack must be available before Test evidence supports staging-entry review beyond planning.
Environment ladder validator implementation is required before automated enforcement can be claimed.
Operator sequence and handoff records are required before promotion workflow readiness can be claimed.
evidenceBoundaries: USF-985 is a Dev-to-Test handoff implementation boundary for promotion claims, not an evidence requirement to bounded local app-surface implementation.
USF-986 is a Test-to-Staging handoff implementation boundary for staging-entry claims, not an evidence requirement to bounded local app-surface implementation.
USF-989 and USF-993 are validator implementation and aggregate wiring boundaries for automated environment-ladder enforcement claims.
USF-982 is covered for bounded local implementation by repository-optimisation-realisation-semantics.json; operator-sequence readiness remains a separate evidence claim.
USF-813 is realised by pre-ui-repository-readiness-realisation.json for bounded local implementation.
validationProofExpectation: Future UI gate must fail closed on unknown environment, unknown provider mode, stale evidence, missing handoff record, generated-report-only proof, or readiness overclaim.
Future staging-entry review cannot be treated as staging readiness or deployment readiness.
Future owner acceptance must be explicit and cannot be inferred from discovery artifacts.
